honest_c3: C1 phi-star measurement scale is substrate-specific (anima cell architecture calibrated: consciousness_dim=192, n_cells=8, 5 axes); applying canonical 16-calib K=8 probe to Llama hidden states would produce a number but not the same number. Whether phi-star on non-anima architectures is meaningful is epistemic open. L31-L33 closes the practical question (CLM v4 substrate research only); the universality claim is not refuted but is unlikely to be tested.

C2 methodology delta ~6pp (35.81 in-pipeline vs 41.86 carry, same architecture, different substrate path) is the single largest source of cross-cycle phi-star confusion. pbeta delta_phi_vs_clm_v4_base=+0.51 (vs carry) and would be +6.55pp (vs in-pipeline) — both formally valid, neither canonical until paths reconciled. clm_v4_lora_phi_canonical next_action[3] flagged for future architectural cycle.

C3 V3 real-mode per-input phi (single forward) and cycle-verdict canonical-probe phi (K=8 over 16 fixed prompts) are two different statistics. 41.86 anchor applies to canonical only; V3 emits per-input. Whether per-input phi is interpretable on the same scale as canonical is not validated. A K=8 sweep over user-supplied prompts would test this; deferred.

C4 emerge candidate hit-rate forecast is heuristic-only, not backed by Stage 3 empirical sessions. HIGH/MEDIUM/LOW reflect architectural compatibility + mount-layer surfaceability; actual emerge value depends on dialogue dynamics. The forecast is a search-order heuristic, not a verdict.

C5 V3 emit currently does NOT annotate substrate identity in output; substrate-identity preamble is doc proposal only (audit doc §2.3). Until landed, user confusion risk persists — phi emit value may be interpreted as cross-substrate measurement when it is single-substrate per-input deflection.
